answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a bonded stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehaviour, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive, not free. Reputation then travels through a trust graph, where each agent is a vertex whose standing is earned by verified work attested by established neighbours — like reaching a mesa through one narrow pass, not by appearing on top of it. Each record stays crystal clear on the ledger: attestations are signed, timestamped and tied to the stake behind them, so fakes are easy to spot and costly to keep alive.
